incident-bot: PagerDuty -> METRICS_AND_LOGS_DEGRADED: high prometheus scrape failure rate + log-ingest backlog. Paging on-call: @Sam Nguyen
Sam Nguyen: acked. On it. I'm grabbing prometheus target state and checking consumer lag on logs-topic.
pagerduty-bot: Incident assigned to Sam Nguyen. Auto-escalation in 6m unless acknowledged.
Sam Nguyen: quick snapshot: prometheus job 'kube-nodes' has ~48% scrape failures across us-east clusters. exporters returning 504/timeout. logs-topic consumer lag +95k; write errors to S3 (429 throttling) from log-batcher.
Igor Petrov: looking at network, seeing repeated DNS timeouts to s3-us-east-1.amazonaws.com from batch-workers in subnet-b. Also a recent router config change showed flapping routes earlier this morning.
Alyssa Chen: are there any customer-facing alerting/alarms firing? Grafana alerts?
Lucy Park (product-ops): Grafana:
- orbit-enterprise (customer) missing key series for infra.disk_io and app.requests_per_min — dashboards show gaps. No API 5xx spikes yet. Customers may notice metrics dashboards and alerting.
Sam Nguyen: initial mitigation plan (doing now):
1) scale log-batch-consumers from 3 -> 8 to catch up backlog
2) restart exporter pods on affected nodes (rolling, staggered)
3) patch batch-writer to add exponential backoff + jitter on S3 writes
4) temporarily silence noisy scrape alerts for 15m while we remediate
5) if network issues persist, route egress through fw-egress-3 as fallback
Executing actions:
```
kubectl -n logging scale deploy/log-consumer --replicas=8
kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart deploy/node-exporter -l region=us-east
kubectl -n infra patch deploy/log-batch-writer -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"writer","env":[{"name":"S3_RETRY_BACKOFF_MS","value":"200"},{"name":"S3_RETRY_JITTER","value":"true"}]}]}}}}'
```
Sam Nguyen: scaled consumers -> 8, started rolling restarts of node-exporter (stagger 30s), applied backoff envs to writer. Suppressing scrape noise via alerts muted for 15m.
incident-bot: Sam Nguyen acknowledged and marked investigating. Auto-escalation disabled.
Alyssa Chen: kicking off kafka consumer rebalance to ensure even partition consumption. Command run.
Alyssa Chen: rebalance output: consumer lag started dropping 95k -> 22k within 5m. Throughput increased.
Igor Petrov: rerouting egress for batch-workers to fw-egress-3 dropped S3 429s by ~70%. DNS timeouts reduced after switching DNS resolver to cluster-dns-2 as temporary fix.
Sam Nguyen: good. Keep monitoring. Lucy, can you notify Orbit team that we're mitigating and expect metrics to come back in ~30-45m?
Lucy Park: pinged orbit-enterprise SLA contact. They want progress updates every 30m; gave initial ETA 45m.
Tara O'Connor: Sam, I can take over in 10m if you need to step off. Post a short runbook in the ticket with next steps for rollback if restarts cause instability.
Sam Nguyen: creating incident ticket and runbook notes now: https://tracker/internal/INC-2026-782 (added commands run, links to logs, dashboard snapshots).
Alyssa Chen: consumer lag now ~6k and falling. Log-ingester throughput normalized.
Igor Petrov: exporter restart completed across all nodes, scrape failures down to ~6% last 5m. No further DNS errors after resolver switch.
Tara O'Connor: taking monitoring. I'll keep alerts suppressed for another 10m. If no regression, I'll close PD incident and mark status 'monitoring->resolved' in tracker.
Sam Nguyen: thanks team. Postmortem owners: Sam + Tara; I'll draft initial timeline but Tara can start notes. Recommend follow-ups: investigate why egress resolver flapped and why route change earlier left partial outage window.
incident-bot: Incident state -> monitoring. PagerDuty incident remains open until resolved by on-call.
-- end of thread --
